title: What the rule guarantees
stimulus: At a fictional arts council, every grant recipient has submitted a project budget. Lena is a grant recipient.
prompt: Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must be true?

choices.text: Lena has submitted a project budget.
choices.explanation: Receiving a grant is sufficient for having submitted a budget under this rule. The rule and Lena's grant status establish this conclusion.

choices.text: Lena has not submitted a project budget.
choices.explanation: This contradicts the stated rule when applied to Lena.

choices.text: The statements leave Lena's budget submission undetermined.
choices.explanation: The grant-recipient fact activates the rule, so budget submission is determined.

choices.text: The statements leave Lena's grant-recipient status undetermined.
choices.explanation: Lena's grant-recipient status is explicitly given.

explanation: Write the rule as grant recipient -> budget submitted. Grant-recipient status is sufficient for budget submission; budget submission is necessary for grant-recipient status. Because Lena satisfies the sufficient condition, the necessary condition must also hold.

title: When a requirement is missing
stimulus: A fictional workshop is open only if a safety officer is present. No safety officer is present now.
prompt: Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must be true now?

choices.text: The workshop is open.
choices.explanation: An open workshop without a safety officer would violate the rule.

choices.text: The workshop is not open.
choices.explanation: The necessary condition is absent. The sufficient condition therefore cannot hold.

choices.text: Whether the workshop is open cannot be determined.
choices.explanation: The contrapositive determines its status: no officer -> not open.

choices.text: A safety officer is present.
choices.explanation: This contradicts the second statement.

explanation: Open only if officer present means open -> officer present. Reverse the order and negate both conditions to form the contrapositive: no officer -> not open. A requirement is not optional when the original rule is assumed true.

title: An effect does not identify its trigger
stimulus: In a fictional sensor system, if smoke is detected, an alarm activates. The alarm has activated. No other rules about the system are given.
prompt: Which statement correctly describes what follows about smoke detection?

choices.text: Smoke was definitely detected.
choices.explanation: This reverses the rule. The rule does not say smoke detection is the only possible trigger.

choices.text: Smoke was definitely not detected.
choices.explanation: Smoke detection is compatible with an activated alarm. Nothing rules it out.

choices.text: Smoke detection cannot be determined from these statements.
choices.explanation: Both smoke detection and no smoke detection are consistent with the activated alarm and the one-way rule.

choices.text: The alarm has not activated.
choices.explanation: This contradicts the observation in the stimulus.

explanation: Smoke detected -> alarm activated does not establish alarm activated -> smoke detected. The necessary condition being true leaves the sufficient condition unresolved. This is a logical rule for the fictional exercise, not advice about real alarm equipment.

title: A requirement is not a guarantee
stimulus: Anyone who enters a fictional archive has completed orientation. Noor has completed orientation. No other information about Noor's entry is given.
prompt: Which statement is supported by the information?

choices.text: Noor has definitely entered the archive.
choices.explanation: Completing a necessary condition does not guarantee entry. That would reverse the rule.

choices.text: Noor has definitely not entered the archive.
choices.explanation: Entry is possible under these facts; no statement excludes it.

choices.text: Noor has not completed orientation.
choices.explanation: The stimulus explicitly says Noor completed orientation.

choices.text: Whether Noor entered the archive remains undetermined.
choices.explanation: Noor may or may not have entered. Both possibilities satisfy entry -> orientation completed.

explanation: The rule is entry -> orientation completed. Orientation is necessary for entry, not sufficient on the information given. Meeting a requirement is compatible with an outcome, but does not by itself establish that outcome.

title: The missing trigger
stimulus: In a fictional file system, every archived file is encrypted. File K is not archived. No further facts about encryption are provided.
prompt: What can be concluded about File K?

choices.text: Its encryption status cannot be determined.
choices.explanation: The rule constrains archived files. It allows a non-archived file to be either encrypted or unencrypted.

choices.text: It is definitely unencrypted.
choices.explanation: This negates both parts without reversing them: the inverse error.

choices.text: It is definitely encrypted.
choices.explanation: Encryption is possible, but the facts do not guarantee it for File K.

choices.text: It is archived.
choices.explanation: This contradicts File K's stated status.

explanation: Archived -> encrypted does not imply not archived -> not encrypted. When the sufficient condition is absent, this rule alone says nothing decisive about the necessary condition. The valid contrapositive instead begins with not encrypted.

title: Connect two conditions
stimulus: In a fictional club, every member has library access. Anyone with library access has a valid card.

choices.text: Every valid-card holder is a member.
choices.explanation: This reverses the direction of the combined rules. A valid-card holder need not be a member.

choices.text: Every member has a valid card.
choices.explanation: Membership guarantees access, which guarantees a valid card. The two arrows can be connected in order.

choices.text: Anyone who is not a member lacks a valid card.
choices.explanation: This is the inverse of the combined rule. Non-members may still hold valid cards.

choices.text: Every valid-card holder has library access.
choices.explanation: This reverses the second rule. A valid card is a requirement for access, not a guarantee of it.

explanation: Member -> library access and library access -> valid card combine to give member -> valid card. Connect arrows only when the conclusion of one matches the condition of the next. The reverse chain is not supplied.
